_comment: OSA event triggers — copy to ~/.osa/TRIGGERS.json. A trigger runs a job when an event happens. Each trigger needs: id, name, event, type ('agent' with a 'job' string, or 'command' with a 'command' string), and enabled. There are two ways a trigger fires: (1) INTERNAL BUS — set 'event' to one of OSA's built-in bus events (listed in _valid_bus_events) and the trigger auto-runs whenever that event occurs; (2) EXTERNAL WEBHOOK — POST a JSON body to http://<host>:9089/webhooks/<id> and the trigger whose 'id' matches runs, no matter what 'event' says. For externally-fired triggers 'event' is just a label; a label that is not a built-in bus event logs one harmless 'unknown event' warning when the trigger is enabled and otherwise does nothing. Job templates support {{payload}} (the whole payload as JSON), {{payload.key}} (a single top-level field), and {{timestamp}}. A trigger that fails 3 times in a row is auto-disabled (circuit breaker).

triggers._note: INTERNAL BUS trigger: runs whenever a messaging channel connects.
triggers.name: Greet on Channel Connect
triggers.job: A channel just connected: {{payload}}. Post a short hello and a one-line note of what I can help with.

triggers._note: INTERNAL BUS trigger: reacts to a critical (algedonic) alert raised inside OSA.
triggers.name: Critical Alert Responder
triggers.job: A critical alert fired at {{timestamp}}: {{payload}}. Investigate the likely cause, check recent activity, and write findings to ~/.osa/alerts/critical.md

triggers._note: INTERNAL BUS trigger: a shell command that logs whenever a runaway agent loop is halted.
triggers.name: Doom Loop Logger

triggers._note: EXTERNAL WEBHOOK trigger: fire it with a POST to http://<host>:9089/webhooks/new-lead and a JSON body. The 'event' value is only a label here.
triggers.name: New Lead Handler
triggers.job: A new lead came in: {{payload}}. Research the company, score the lead 1-10, and draft a personalized first response. Save it to ~/.osa/leads/{{payload.id}}.md

triggers._note: EXTERNAL WEBHOOK trigger: fire it from CI with a POST to http://<host>:9089/webhooks/deploy-notify.
triggers.name: Deployment Notification
